clue.text: Means to open case to nick Colombian criminal

indicators.note: criminal works as a description of the fodder: its letters are crooked, bent out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Colombian crook breaks into a safe to steal from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun naming the Colombian, but it is the anagram signal for TO NICK plus COLOMBIAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A coded dial mechanism is a way to open a safe or briefcase without a key.

clue.text: Thong for a revealing entertainer

parts.note: a thong is a narrow strip of leather
per means for each, for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: A skimpy undergarment worn by a performer who shows off a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic dancer who takes clothes off is an entertainer who reveals a great deal.

clue.text: Poor father's opening junk mail

parts.note: bum as an adjective means of poor quality, as in 'a bum deal'

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from father's

explanation.surface: A struggling dad's first job is opening a pile of unwanted post.
explanation.walkthrough: BUMF is British slang for useless paperwork or circulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for unwanted printed material such as leaflets and circulars.

clue.text: Disciplined old criminal to stop breaking in

indicators.note: breaking in signals that one word forces its way into the middle of another

parts.note: bent is slang for corrupt or criminal
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A veteran crook tries to halt a burglary in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun for the old crook, but it is an adjective, as is the slang sense of 'bent' it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-trained, compliant person does as told, which is what a disciplined one does.

clue.text: Boxes in deserted farmhouse containing stuff to go to Sweden

indicators.note: containing says the emptied word holds the other pieces within it
deserted means emptied, so the farmhouse loses all its inside letters and keeps only its ends

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Crates in an abandoned farmhouse hold belongings due to be shipped to Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to box something in is to surround it with a border, as a picture is framed.

clue.text: Takes in cover and old sheet

parts.note: to take someone in is to deceive or fool them
a cap is a cover or lid

explanation.surface: Someone tucks in a blanket and an aged bedsheet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional British paper size, larger than A4, now largely obsolete.

clue.text: Left one building up steps

parts.note: someone who adds things up, building a total, is an adder

explanation.surface: One person left on a building site, going up the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing frame of rungs is a set of portable steps.

clue.text: Presents left in sock: girl's excited

indicators.note: excited suggests agitated, stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: A girl is thrilled by the gifts left for her in a Christmas stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly a definition of the answer, but the letters of LEFT IN SOCK GIRLS must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Small gifts tucked into a Christmas stocking are presents.

clue.text: Have more than old-fashioned dress?

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a number is a dress or outfit, as in 'a little black number'

explanation.surface: Is a dated frock simply having too much?
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in quantity is to have more of something than a rival.

clue.text: Love role in moving pictures?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: A romantic part in a film, the kind of moving pictures at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving pictures' suggests films, but here it means images that seem to move: optical art plays tricks on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical art uses patterns that create an illusion of motion, so its pictures appear to shift.

clue.text: Initially, bid's rejected — is estate agent told?

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the words that follow are taken

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent of the FBI

explanation.surface: A buyer's offer has been turned down: has the estate agent been informed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate agent' reads as one phrase, but 'estate' gives its first letter and 'agent' alone is the FBI man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been given instructions or information beforehand has been informed.

clue.text: See: doctor to nurse is sweet

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so the doctor's word cradles the other piece

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Look: the doctor coming to tend a patient is lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneful music is sweet to the ear.

clue.text: Spread out cycling? Absolutely not

indicators.note: cycling means the letters go round, the last one moving to the front

parts.note: to open something is to spread it out, as a map

explanation.surface: Fanned out on a bike ride? Certainly not.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial, emphatic no is a flat refusal.

clue.text: Dog chew girl's thrown to save ball

indicators.note: to save is to keep safe, so the rearranged letters hold the ball within them
thrown suggests tossed about, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A dog chews a toy that a girl threw, keeping hold of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges CHEW GIRLS into WELSHCRGI, and 'to save' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged herding breed from Wales, famously favoured by the Queen.

clue.text: Curse as no room squeezing into big top?

indicators.note: squeezing into says the pieces are pushed inside another word

parts.note: a circus big top is a large tent
no is zero, shaped like the letter O
RM is the abbreviation for room, as in property listings

explanation.surface: Swearing because there's no space when crowding into the circus tent.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a curse can be an affliction or source of great suffering, just like constant anguish.

clue.text: Sailor forgetting pop on ship: might one go on the lash?

definitions.text: might one go on the lash?

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving something out, so the named letters are dropped

parts.note: Popeye is the cartoon sailor man
pop is taken as written, the letters removed
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A seaman going off his fizzy drink on board ship, perhaps heading for a drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on the lash' is British slang for a night of heavy drinking, but here the lash is an eyelash.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up pencilled along the eyelid sits on the base of the eyelashes.

clue.text: Secretly listening to Prince during recording

indicators.note: during means the prince comes in the middle of the recording

parts.note: taping is recording

explanation.surface: Spying on a royal while making a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping a phone line is covert eavesdropping.

clue.text: Dancing and moving behind beat

indicators.note: behind says the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
going means moving

explanation.surface: A dancer swaying and moving to the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing the Argentine ballroom dance is one particular kind of dancing.

clue.text: Wearing coat he is perverted and immature

parts.note: if you are in a coat you are wearing it

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a coat is a pervert, and childish too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only just begun and not yet fully formed is undeveloped.

clue.text: Drunk hen to flash bust

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: a blink is a flash, as in 'in the blink of an eye'

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman on a hen night exposes her chest.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British bride-to-be's night out; 'bust' looks like a chest but means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget that is malfunctioning or broken is said to be faulty.

clue.text: Plastic felt over bottom of pan

definitions.text: Plastic felt over bottom of pan

indicators.note: plastic means pliable, easily remoulded, so these letters take a new shape

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A synthetic layer coats the base of a frying pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the non-stick coating is a plastic spread over the bottom of a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: This trade-name polymer is the non-stick coating applied to cookware.

clue.text: Trump excuse

definitions.meaning: in British slang to trump is to break wind, to fart
to excuse someone is to spare them a punishment

explanation.surface: A political name paired with forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing wind and pardoning an offender are both expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Ace American's one nicking intro from Chuck Berry

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, so the stolen letter goes inside

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
A is the abbreviation for American; read as American has
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A top American musician steals the opening of a Chuck Berry song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck Berry' reads as the rock-and-roll star, but Berry is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple fruit of an Amazon palm is sold as a health food berry.

clue.text: Red felt tip's missing top, finally running out

indicators.note: running out suggests ink spreading, so the remaining letters are rearranged
missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the pen's letters
finally means the last letter of the word top is the one to remove

explanation.surface: A red marker pen has lost its cap and is running dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing top' looks like a lost cap, but 'finally' takes the last letter of top, P; 'running out' rearranges FELTTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Red is a political left-winger, a socialist or communist.

clue.text: To have ambition is a self-inflicted disadvantage

parts.note: to own something is to have it
a goal is an ambition

explanation.surface: Being ambitious ends up harming yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, scoring in your own net is a mistake that hurts your side, hence any self-harming act.

clue.text: Want date on evening to turn up

indicators.note: to turn up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top
on says the first piece sits above the second in this down entry

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening

explanation.surface: Longing for a date to appear in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To require or lack something is to be in want of it.

clue.text: Cold? Warmth in small bulb

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
love is warmth of feeling

explanation.surface: Chilly? A little heat in a tiny light bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulb' suggests a lamp, but it is a bulb of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment of a garlic head is one of the small bulbs that make up the whole.

clue.text: Cool character that's written for star

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A calm personality is what's written into a celebrity's script.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirers send mail to celebrities, so such correspondence is written for a star.
